asf-map72-322.summary: After Soliers' recall, an informant (code .51.) says the King will send an ambassador to Rome as soon as Rocciafort arrives, believed to be the bishop of 'Lancres', empowered to negotiate everything with the Pope, and foresees the same quarrel as the Pope's with the bishop of Marseille; after Alfonso Ariosti's visit for Ferrara, the King asked that the Venetian ambassador be approached so that Venice give back Monselice, Este and Montagnana, held by the Este as imperial fiefs.
asf-map72-322.en:
From the reading by sense (reading322.md); {x} probable, ‹…› unresolved, [x] supplied for English only. About 77% of the cipher words read: the gaps are real.

Block 1. And ‹.51.› has told {us} that, as soon as Rocciafort has arrived {here}, there {will be sent} to you a man as {ambassador} of this Majesty [the King], who we {believe} will be the {bishop} of {"Lancres"}, {having} {settled} before his departure from here that {this} Majesty ‹…› [he may] negotiate {everything} ‹…› {His Holiness}; with whom ‹.51.› believes that {in truth} ‹…› the same quarrel {will} arise as the one there {is} at present {between} His {Holiness} and {Monsignore} of {Marseille}.

Block 2. [He] will {have} had {made known} to you the {commission} he carries ‹…› ‹…› on {every?} occasion ‹…›.

Block 3.

asf-map72-307.summary: Pandolfini cannot name the Swiss friends of France (secrecy, danger in their cantons); the King's envoy found the Swiss obstinate, offended that he entered without a safe-conduct; the Archduke's embassy led by the count of Nassau presses the marriage of Madame Renee; the renewal of the English accord is expected; the King wants the Italian enterprise 'con grossissime forze', but reason forbids it this year; nothing yet on the truce with Spain.
asf-map72-307.en:
From the reading by sense (reading307.md). The gaps are real; {x} probable and ‹…› unresolved are in the Italian reading.

Copy of Francesco Pandolfini's letter to the Otto di Pratica, Paris, 16 February 1515 (per no. 313, written early on the day
of Francis I's solemn entry into Paris). (1) The Otto had asked who the Swiss was who came to court and which friends of the French had sent him: Pandolfini answers
that this is no longer needed and that he could not name them, the matter being kept very secret because of the danger those men
would run in their cantons. (2) On the man the King sent to the Swiss (letter of 13 January): he has it from a good source that the
envoy, who went with a mandate from ‹…›, found the Swiss obstinate; they told him they marvelled at his presumption in entering their
country without a safe-conduct (rest partly unread). (3) A short passage unread.

asf-map72-309.summary: As proof of the King's goodwill, Louise of Savoy offered the papal orator a marriage of the Duke of Valentinois's daughter (Louise Borgia) for Lorenzo; the King awaits the Pope's declaration on the newly made league to learn his mind. A Borgia match for Lorenzo is mentioned in the literature; this offer of Feb 1515 is still to be checked in the printed sources.
asf-map72-309.en:
From the reading by sense (reading309.md). The gaps are real; {x} probable and ‹…› unresolved are in the Italian reading.

Letter from Francesco Pandolfini, Florentine orator at the French court, to Lorenzo de' Medici, Paris, 26 February 1515. In clear
he refers Lorenzo to the enclosed copy of his letter to the Otto (no. 310) and assures him of the King's good disposition towards
the Pope, Florence and the Medici. The cipher passages add: (A) proof of it, besides the King's words, are the offers Madame
d'Angoulême (Louise of Savoy) made a few days ago to the papal orator, about the ".48.", of a marriage between the daughter of the
Duke of Valentinois (Louise Borgia) and Lorenzo himself; (B) the King is eager to see what resolution and declaration the Pope will
make regarding the newly concluded league, from which he expects to learn the Pope's real mind towards him.

asf-map72-310.summary: La Guiche ('Ghiscia'), the King's ambassador in England, came back to settle the articles and left again; Suffolk says the accord will be made; a Spanish friar-bishop met at Calais goes to England to 'set fire', in vain; the Flemings ask for Madame Renee on dishonest terms; the King has a copy of the league and is satisfied with the Pope; the accord with England will be confirmed, Scotland pending; a Swiss diet plans to attack France; the King considers hiring troops (code .22.); the Catholic King proposes a three-year truce, fearing for Naples and Castile.
asf-map72-310.en:
From the reading by sense (reading310.md). The gaps are real; {x} probable and ‹…› unresolved are in the Italian reading.

Copy of Pandolfini's letter to the Otto, Paris, 26 February 1515, continued on 27 February and 2 March. (A) Monsieur de La Guiche, the King's
ambassador in England with the First President of Rouen, came back to court to settle the articles under negotiation and has left again for
England; the Duke of Suffolk and the other English envoys in Paris say the accord will be made in any case. La Guiche met at Calais a friar, a
Spanish bishop, on his way to England to "set fire"; Suffolk, very pro-French, answered that he would not succeed. (B) The Flemish envoys ask
for the marriage of Madame Renée on such dishonest terms that, according to a councillor, nothing will come of it; the demands are thought to
be made with artifice and on the Emperor's orders.

asf-map72-311.summary: Rumour of the Duke of Suffolk's marriage to the 'white queen' Mary Tudor; letters from Rome of the 24th say the Pope and Florence joined the new league; Pandolfini asked the King not to believe it, and the King said he would not believe it until he saw it; P.S.: the league would pay 30,000 ducats a month to the Swiss and 30,000 to the Viceroy, shared by the Pope and two members coded .16. and .17.
asf-map72-311.en:
From the reading by sense (reading311.md). The gaps are real; {x} probable and ‹…› unresolved are in the Italian reading.

Continuation ("kept back to the 4th", March 1515) of a letter from Pandolfini to the Otto, sent via Lyon. (A) The court will not leave
Paris until the agreement with England is concluded. (B) There is talk that the Duke of Suffolk will marry the "white queen" Mary
Tudor, Louis XII's widow; the rumour is growing and English members of the queen's household complain of it. (C) Letters from Rome of
the 24th report, from a sure source, that the Pope and the Florentine Signoria have joined the newly concluded league; the news is all
over the court. At the request of the Florentine consul in Lyon, Pandolfini asked the King not to believe it; the King answered that,
given Florence's loyalty to the Crown, he would not believe it until he saw it.

asf-map72-333.summary: Little of weight to report from the French court; everything hangs on the decisions to be taken in Rome, awaited with very great suspicion. Content already given in clear by 332 (copy to the Otto of the same day).
asf-map72-333.en:
From the reading by sense (reading333.md). Every word read; the content is also given in clear in 332.

Pandolfini to Lorenzo de' Medici, Paris, 27 December 1514: he writes only to send the copy of his letter to the Otto. In cipher: on
this side (the French court) there is little of weight to report for now; everything hangs on the decisions to be taken "there" (in
Rome), which are awaited here with very great suspicion.
Full translation of the cipher block: "On this side there is at present little of moment to report, everything depending on the resolutions that will be taken there [in Rome], about which we are here in very great suspicion."

system: Consonant signs with the vowel written as a superscript figure (1-5 = u, o, i, e, a), bare vowel signs, homophones, word signs (F = et, M = non, T = senza) and a numeric nomenclator between points (.2. papa, .4. Cristianissimo, .64. Santita), between clear…
